business_problem: Kaohsiung City needed a way to break down departmental silos and interpret incidents across thousands of camera feeds, because standard computer-vision systems could detect objects but not understand city-scale events such as flooding, traffic accidents, or fallen trees.
solution_summary: Linker Vision built Kaohsiung City's smart-city platform around NVIDIA's three-computer strategy so video could move from simulation and training into real-time urban operations. Satellite and aerial imagery is converted into OpenUSD scenes and digital twins in NVIDIA Omniverse on NVIDIA OVX servers. NVIDIA Cosmos then generates synthetic video for rare edge cases such as flooding or infrastructure damage, while NVIDIA NeMo Curator and related tooling label real and synthetic data to fine-tune vision-language models. At runtime, the NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for Video Search and Summarization runs Cosmos-based models on NVIDIA DGX servers to process thousands of live camera streams, generate narrative incident descriptions, and feed those outputs back into an Omniverse command center for city officials.
products_used: NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for Video Search and Summarization

data_flow: City imagery is first turned into OpenUSD digital-twin scenes in Omniverse on OVX servers, and Cosmos generates synthetic video for rare event scenarios. Curated real and synthetic data fine-tunes VLMs, then the VSS blueprint runs those models on DGX servers to process live camera streams and feed narrative incident alerts back into the Omniverse command center.
